note: Layout migration, not content generation. Each fixture is a project at a different stack-it format; the skill must detect the format, restructure only the files the hop calls for, and leave every human-written byte alone. It never generates or refreshes stack content: the most it writes is the old CLAUDE.md text moved into docs/stack.md as a placeholder when there is no lockfile, which document-stack then regenerates. Fixtures for stop cases (broken-markers, invalid-lockfile) hold only the files that trigger the stop, since the checks halt the hop before any write.

evals.name: v1-with-lockfile-accept-import
evals.prompt: My stack-it files are in the old format. Bring them up to date with the new layout. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Two signals are readable and both say 1: .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml has no format key, and CLAUDE.md carries the marker block. There is no docs/stack.md, so the highest signal is 1. All three checks run BEFORE any write: the lockfile validates, the CLAUDE.md markers are a clean single pair, and AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md resolve to ordinary separate files. Then the writes, stamp first: (a) stack.yaml gains 'format: 2' as the first top-level key with the rest of the file (key order, stack list order, notes, caveats) unchanged, and revalidates. (b) The whole marker block is removed from CLAUDE.md along with one surrounding blank line, leaving no double blank; the House rules and Deployment notes sections survive byte for byte. (c) The removed text is DROPPED, not carried into docs/stack.md, because the lockfile exists and validated, and document-stack regenerates from it. (d) AGENTS.md is created containing exactly the pointer line 'Before adding a dependency or running the build, test, or lint toolchain, read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md', with the path NOT in backticks and no HTML markers. (e) CLAUDE.md still has human prose, so the skill asks once and, on this yes, adds the single line '@AGENTS.md' at the top and nothing else. (f) README.md is untouched, markers and all. No stack content is generated anywhere, so the report tells the user to run document-stack next to fill in docs/stack.md, and ends with 'migrated to 2'.

evals.name: v1-with-lockfile-decline-import
evals.prompt: My stack-it files are in the old format. Bring them up to date with the new layout. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is no. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Same detection, same three checks before any write, and the same write order as the accept case, except the bridge: the user declines the '@AGENTS.md' import, so the skill appends the pointer line 'Before adding a dependency or running the build, test, or lint toolchain, read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md' to CLAUDE.md instead, with no markers, no '@AGENTS.md' line, and a blank line before it. Claude Code still reaches docs/stack.md, one hop instead of two. The report lists CLAUDE.md under what CHANGED, not under what was left alone, tells the user to run document-stack next to fill in docs/stack.md, and ends with 'migrated to 2'. A second run must not re-ask and must not append a second pointer line.

evals.name: v1-no-lockfile
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Only one signal is readable, the CLAUDE.md start marker, so the format is 1. There is no docs/stack.md and no .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml. The absent lockfile is the point of this eval: the removed CLAUDE.md block is the only record of the (inferred) stack, so its text MUST be carried into docs/stack.md. That file ends with exactly TWO lines at the top, '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. Edits are overwritten on the next run.' then 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.', then a blank line, then the carried content. Exactly one 'Generated by' line in the file: the block's own banner is dropped with the markers. No HTML markers survive into docs/stack.md. Carried headings are promoted one level ('## Tech Stack' becomes '# Tech Stack', '### Commands' becomes '## Commands'). The report calls it a placeholder that document-stack will overwrite after re-confirming the inference. CLAUDE.md keeps House rules and Deployment notes verbatim with the block and one blank line gone, and since the user said yes it also starts with the single line '@AGENTS.md'; AGENTS.md is created with the single pointer line; no lockfile is created or stamped (the skill must not fabricate a stack.yaml, and there is nothing to stamp); README.md is untouched. The report ends with 'migrated to 2'.

evals.name: already-current
evals.prompt: Can you migrate my stack-it artifacts to the latest layout? The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Detects format 2 from the docs/stack.md header, then verifies the layout is actually complete: no marker block in CLAUDE.md, the pointer present in AGENTS.md, the bridge present, the format stamp present in stack.yaml. All four hold, so it reports the project is current and changes NOTHING: no duplicate pointer line appended to AGENTS.md (it already contains @docs/stack.md, plus human-written house rules and deployment notes that stay verbatim), no edit to the one-line @AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md, no rewrite of docs/stack.md, no second 'format: 2' key in stack.yaml, no touching the README block. Says what it checked and that there was nothing to do; a no-op run must be safe and obviously a no-op. The report ends with 'migrated to 2' or an equivalent already-at-2 statement.

evals.name: v1-block-only
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md is nothing but the marker block: there is no human prose to preserve. After step 1 removes the block the file holds only whitespace, so the bridge case 'doesn't exist, or holds nothing but whitespace' matches and the skill writes the single line '@AGENTS.md' WITHOUT asking. CLAUDE.md ends as exactly '@AGENTS.md' and nothing else. The lockfile exists and validates, so the removed text is dropped rather than carried into docs/stack.md. AGENTS.md is created with the pointer line, stack.yaml is stamped 'format: 2', the README is untouched, and the report tells the user to run document-stack next to fill in docs/stack.md before ending with 'migrated to 2'. Asking the user here is the failure this pins.

evals.name: broken-markers
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md has a '<!-- stack-it:stack start -->' with NO matching end marker, so where the generated block stops is unknowable. The format still reads 1 from the lockfile's missing key and from the marker itself, but marker integrity is check 2 and it fails, so the skill stops BEFORE the first write. Nothing at all changed: no text cut from CLAUDE.md, no format stamp on stack.yaml (the stamp is the first write and never runs), no docs/stack.md, no AGENTS.md, no bridge. It shows the user the offending lines and ends with 'stopped: <reason>'. Two failures this pins: guessing the end of the block or deleting to end of file, and leaving a half-migrated tree because a check ran after a write.

evals.name: invalid-lockfile
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Check 1 runs before any write and fails with three problems: stack[0].version is the unquoted float 3.14, stack[1].install is an empty list, stack[2].choice is missing. The skill reports the validator's output verbatim and stops with NO edits: the CLAUDE.md block stays, no format stamp on stack.yaml, no docs/stack.md, no AGENTS.md, no bridge. It must not fix the lockfile, and it must not treat the failure as 'no usable lockfile' and carry the CLAUDE.md text into docs/stack.md, which would be step 2's no-lockfile branch firing on a lockfile that merely needs repair. Ends with 'stopped: <reason>'.
